{{Short description|Greek mathematician (1878–1928)}}
[[File:Georgios Remoundos.jpg|thumb|Georgios Remoundos]]
'''Georgios Remoundos''' (Γεώργιος Ρεμούνδος, 1878 in Athens – 27 April 1928) was a Greek mathematician and a founding member of the [[Academy of Athens (modern)|Academy of Athens]] in 1926.

After graduating from the [[Varvakeio]], he studied at the [[University of Athens]] and was given a government scholarship to study in France. He studied at the [[École Normale Supérieure]] and then at the [[University of Paris]], where he received in 1905 his Ph.D. (Thèse de doctorat) with thesis ''Sur les zéros d'une classe de fonctions transcendantes''.<ref>[http://www.sudoc.abes.fr/xslt//DB=2.1/SET=1/TTL=1/SHW?FRST=2 ''Sur les zéros d'une classe de fonctions transcendantes'', (Thèse de doctorat) by G. Rémoundos, 1905, SUDOC]</ref>
A post-doctoral student of [[Émile Picard]], Remoundos published in French under the name "Georges J. Rémoundos". He was a professor of mathematics at the University of Athens.<ref>[http://data.bnf.fr/12570187/georges_remoundos/ Georges Rémoundos (1878–1928) – Author – Resources from the BnF]</ref> He was a co-editor and co-founder, along with [[Panagiotis Zervos|P. Zervos]], N. Sakellarios, and K. Lambiris, of the journal ''Bulletin de la Société Mathématique de Gréce'', first published in May 1919 written about one-third in French and two-thirds in Greek.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Articles in Current Periodicals|journal=The American Mathematical Monthly|volume=27|issue= 7/9 for Jul.–Sep|pages=314–319|year=1920|jstor=2972261}}</ref> Remoundos was three times an [[invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]]: in 1908 at Rome, in 1912 at Cambridge (England), and in 1920 at Strasbourg.<ref>{{cite book|chapter-url=http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1920/Main/icm1920.0205.0211.ocr.pdf|pages=205–211|year=1921|title=Compte rendu du Congrès international des mathématiciens tenu à Strasbourg du 22 au 30 Septembre 1920|chapter=''Sur le module et les zéros des functions analytiques'' by Georges J. Rémoundos}}</ref>
